dek: Fuerza Regida led with eight wins and Bad Bunny took Artist of the Year, but Bronx-born Romeo and Royce ruled tropical.

slides.label: The night
slides.text: The *2026 Billboard Latin Music Awards* took over Miami's James L. Knight Center on *Oct. 22*, live on Telemundo and Peacock, hosted by Carmen Villalobos and Javier Poza.

slides.label: The leader
slides.text: *Fuerza Regida* won *eight* awards, four from "Marlboro Rojo" alone, plus Billboard's *Vanguard Award* for pushing regional Mexican music onto the global stage.

slides.label: The king
slides.text: *Bad Bunny* won seven, including *Artist of the Year*, Tour of the Year and Songwriter of the Year. Hola reports he did not even attend.

slides.label: The field
slides.text: Karol G, Peso Pluma and Romeo Santos won *four* each. Karol G took the first-ever *Fan Artist* award, and Rosalía entered the *Billboard Hall of Fame*.

slides.label: The Bronx
slides.text: Bronx-born *Romeo Santos* and *Prince Royce* won Tropical Song and Latin Airplay Song for "Lokita Por Mí," plus Top Tropical Album. Santos took *Tropical Artist of the Year*.

slides.label: The album
slides.text: "Better Late Than Never" dropped as a surprise on Nov. 28, 2025: *13 tracks*, no advance singles. The Boston Globe says they worked on it in secret for *seven years*.

slides.label: The map
slides.text: Regional Mexican is the *streaming engine*. Omar Courtz won *New Artist of the Year*, and Burna Boy took Crossover Artist, proof Afrobeats and Latin keep *borrowing from each other*.

slides.label: The Den's take
slides.text: Fuerza Regida and Bad Bunny won the scoreboard. Respect. But the New York moment is two *Bronx-born bachateros* who took their time. *Better late than never*, indeed.

cta_line: Now bring them to *a New York stage*.

Karol G, Peso Pluma and Romeo Santos won four each, and Karol G took the first Fan Artist award. Romeo Santos and Prince Royce won Tropical Song and Latin Airplay Song for "Lokita Por Mí" and Top Tropical Album for "Better Late Than Never," the surprise album the Boston Globe says they made in secret over seven years. Santos also took Tropical Artist of the Year.

The wider map: regional Mexican drives streaming, Omar Courtz won New Artist of the Year, and Burna Boy took Crossover Artist.

caption_linkedin:
The 2026 Billboard Latin Music Awards were a snapshot of where Latin music's audience and money are moving.

Fuerza Regida led with eight awards, four for one song, "Marlboro Rojo," and earned the Vanguard Award for taking regional Mexican music global. Bad Bunny won Artist of the Year without attending. Burna Boy's Crossover Artist win points to a widening overlap between Afrobeats and Latin audiences.

The brand lesson came from tropical. Bronx-born Romeo Santos and Prince Royce released "Better Late Than Never" as a surprise, 13 tracks with no advance singles, after years of work, and won Top Tropical Album. Sometimes the strongest partnership is the obvious one, executed patiently.
